content:
Apple has officially launched advertising on Apple Maps, and will gradually expand it over the next few weeks. Here are the details.

Advertising on Apple Maps has officially launched in the United States and Canada.

Apple announced earlier this year that Maps would begin including ads in the United States and Canada this summer. With September approaching, the relevant time window is about to end.

However, Apple has officially reached its goal: Apple Maps has now officially included ads.

Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that ads on Maps began rolling out over the past few days and will continue to expand to all users over the coming weeks.

Within the Maps app, ads will appear in two places:

  • Before searching: Ads will appear in the "Suggested Locations" section of the search screen.
  • After searching: Ads will be displayed in search results where relevant.

Ads look the same as other business information, just with an additional small blue label that says "Ad". You can see an example of the ad in the image above.

The most popular comment is from Steve

The Apple App Store experience has become terrible because of the ads, so I'll try to minimize my time there—search online first for what I want, then go in. Looks like Maps will use the same trick. Annoying users just to earn a bit more money is a poor strategy. Next up: stickers and pre-installed bloatware?

As with Apple's advertising policies for its other services, the company emphasizes that Maps ads protect user privacy. According to Apple Newsroom:
